messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Parental genotypes tetraploid genetic map construction
parts:
R/qtl is designed for diploid organisms, and for crosses between inbred lines. In an F2 intercross between two inbred strains, the offspring would have genotype AA, AB, or BB, with the parents being A and B. 

From SNP genotypes, parents would be either 0 or 2 and offspring 0, 1, or 2. You’d take all SNPs where A parent is 0 and B parent is 2 and recode the offspring as 0 → AA, 1 → AB, 2 → BB. For SNPs where A parent is 2 and B parent is 0, you’d recode the offspring as 0 → BB, 1 → AB, 2 → AA. 

In the case of outbred parents, you also have cases where one or the other parent is heterozygous. And to handle these in R/qtl you also need to have inferred phase. Really, R/qtl doesn’t quite have the facilities for doing map construction in an outbred F2. 

With tetraploids, don’t you need dosages at the SNPs? It’s not just 0,1,2.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Parental genotypes tetraploid genetic map construction
parts:
All of my general thoughts on map construction have been incorporated into 

   https://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/geneticmaps.pdf

If segregation distortion is common, then by omitting markers that depart from 1:2:1 segregation, you may be left only with markers on one chromosome. I wouldn’t want to remove more than a small proportion of markers due to segregation distortion until I have a map established.

You could try switching to markerlrt() in place of est.rf(), to measure association between markers prior to using formLinkageGroups().

Karl

If segregation distortion is common, then by omitting markers that depart from 1:2:1 segregation, you may be left only with markers on one chromosome. I wouldn’t want to remove more than a small proportion of markers due to segregation distortion until I have a map established.

On Tuesday, 20 February 2018 15:17:51 UTC+3, Karl Broman wrote:
R/qtl is designed for diploid organisms, and for crosses between inbred lines. In an F2 intercross between two inbred strains, the offspring would have genotype AA, AB, or BB, with the parents being A and B. 

From SNP genotypes, parents would be either 0 or 2 and offspring 0, 1, or 2. You’d take all SNPs where A parent is 0 and B parent is 2 and recode the offspring as 0 → AA, 1 → AB, 2 → BB. For SNPs where A parent is 2 and B parent is 0, you’d recode the offspring as 0 → BB, 1 → AB, 2 → AA. 

In the case of outbred parents, you also have cases where one or the other parent is heterozygous. And to handle these in R/qtl you also need to have inferred phase. Really, R/qtl doesn’t quite have the facilities for doing map construction in an outbred F2. 

With tetraploids, don’t you need dosages at the SNPs? It’s not just 0,1,2.

karl
